There's a few things to say here about this movie.

First, the movie is based on a series of comic books/manga of the same name.  When the movie started production, the last book of the series (potentially the last two books depending on how long the movie was in production) had not been written yet.  This led to the movie having a tough time with the ending, as well as not having a good idea what was absolutely necessary to highlight in the earlier portions of the story to make the ending make sense.  The director of the movie did consult with the author of the books, but it was an imperfect system.

Second, and somewhat related to the first, the last book in the book series is really important to highlighting what the overall story is about.  A large portion of that book is dedicated to laying out Scott Pilgrim has been a pretty awful person for the few books of the series (and a good stretch of time before that).  And once Scott realizes he's been awful, he starts working to be a better person, make amends with the people his wronged, and actually act like an adult.  It makes the whole self-actualization arc feel much more earned instead of a bit of a throw-in at the end of the movie.

Third, the original series of comic books is six books long, and these are not tiny little comics that are 20 pages each.  These are each stand alone books that are ~200 pages each.  To put it short, they were trying to cram an absolute metric ton of content into a 2 hour runtime.  The pacing of the movie is at best breathless, and it isn't surprising to me that someone who isn't already familiar with the story upfront might get a bit lost/confused at parts as stuff just seems to happen.  The movie probably should have been 3 hours long (or even an HBO miniseries instead), but they had to crop it to 2 hours, likely for commercialization reasons.

Scott Pilgrim vs. The World is a definitely a unique movie in its aesthetics and style, and I wholly believe that the actors and director did their damnedest to move the material work as well as it could.  But I think they made a few fundamental mistakes in the production of the movie, and that leads the movie to being this flawed cult classic instead of a timeless blockbuster.

Yeah Scott being unlikeable is kind of the point, that's why the first thing that they tell you is that he's dating a high schooler. It's about that period in your life where you're not a teenager any more but you're not quite capable of functioning like a true adult. People mess up and treat others badly in the name of finding themselves and learning their needs. 

The pacing is maybe a little strange to first time viewers because the plot points are so close together. One thing to keep in mind is that this is adapting a work that is a multi-book sort of "slice of life" character drama rather than a YA action piece. They had to be pretty selective about what they wanted to put into the movie, and the original series wasn't fully done at the time the movie was made.

You're not really meant to like Scott that much. At its core it's a coming of age movie about someone realising they're a selfish man-child. I love the film, but I do think it's guilty of leaning towards style over substance, but that's mostly because there's _so much_ style. I think later post-Cornetto Edgar Wright films have this problem to a greater detriment, I think SPVTW gets away with it, partly because I personally think the core cast of characters are great
